sections.title: Urban Innovation and Technology
sections.description:
Cities are labs for innovation and testing grounds for new technologies. People, ideas, firms, capital, and technology come together in cities to create powerful forces of agglomeration and make cities engines of economic activity, entrepreneurship, and innovation. At the same time, the very innovations that emerge from cities can transform how cities grow, function, and are experienced. This course explores this two-way relationship: why innovation and entrepreneurship thrive in cities, how new technologies change urban life and development, and how planners can shape the changes they bring.
Through comparative cases, seminar discussions, and project-based learning, students will develop frameworks for understanding and evaluating urban innovation and technological change. They will consider the choices, tradeoffs, and consequences that come with urban innovation and technology issues such as urban innovation districts, smart city initiatives, urban data and artificial intelligence, and connected and autonomous vehicles. Particular attention will be given to the role of planners in navigating social equity, sustainability, accessibility, privacy, governance, and public participation to ensure that technological innovation improves the lives of people who live in cities.
